title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a political impersonation carried out with a generative video tool. The videos were posted to a sitting congressman's own account and presented fake versions of his opponent saying things she never said. The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the tool produced labelled synthetic video, and a person then chose to post it as campaign content.

Catching this required nothing from the model. The clips were labelled as made with Grok Imagine, so the synthetic origin was disclosed on their face. What was absent was any check by the poster or the platform before the material reached an audience, and any mechanism by which the person depicted could correct the record. The response described in the reporting was a legal letter and a further AI video, not a retraction.

The reporting does not establish that the videos were intended to deceive, that any law was broken, or that the cease-and-desist letter produced any change in the account's behaviour. A cease-and-desist letter is an allegation, not a finding, and the campaign's public response is not evidence of intent.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over AI deepfake videos posted to his X account. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. The videos, labeled as made with Grok Imagine, show fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared Aug. 4. Her attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that the content is fiction and could violate state defamation law.

Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring his accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden responded on social media with another AI video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points in 2024.
